after: a faint echo of distance through distinctness
reason: The branch is spatial remoteness, while تَّبَيَّنَ means that evidence has become distinct. Their shared bayn-family leaves a weak separation-to-distance echo, but the verb does not itself mean physical distance.

after: the one who distances them from the recognized way
reason: ش ط ن B001 gives distance and removal from a point; فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ explicitly turns the people away from a named course. That wording activates distance from the good path alongside the ordinary name of the adversary.

after: a distant force set against false claims of nearness
reason: The near-surah word أَوْلِيَآءَ names protectors or allies, a nearness image that can sharpen the opposite distance in this branch. The contrast is available in the surah, though it does not directly describe the adversary's location.

after: an image set opposite kinship and mercy
reason: The proposed raḥm branch hears kinship through الرَّحْمَٰنِ, a closeness image that can oppose ش ط ن B001's distance from good. The Fatiha word ordinarily means the Merciful, so the kinship contrast remains a secondary echo.

after: a faint binding image beside discernment
reason: The branch names fastening with a rope, including tying a camel's foreleg. يَعْقِلُونَ means that people reason, and the traditional bind-to-restrain image behind عقل gives a weak mental-restraint echo rather than a literal rope scene.

after: an image of tightly twisted argument beside twisted cord
reason: ش ط ن B002 gives a tightly twisted, strong cord, and تُجَٰدِلُوٓا۟ names disputing with the People of the Book. The dispute can suggest a verbal tangle, but there is no cord in the verse, so this is only a note.

after: a fragile woven dwelling set beside the rope image
reason: The concept route reaches أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ and the spider's بيت, whose web gives a faint strand image for the long twisted rope branch. A web is not the strong water-drawing rope defined here, so the connection stays tentative.

after: a faint taut-line image alongside the straight path
reason: The Fatiha's ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ names a straight course, which can call the line-like shape of a taut rope. The branch means a long well-rope and its binding use, so straightness alone only weakly activates it.

after: the force that diverts people from their intended direction
reason: ش ط ن B003 gives turning someone away from the direction they intend. فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ states that the people were turned from the way, directly activating that directional sense.

before: the one who turns people from a course,
after: a force opposed to the stated worshipful direction
reason: The nearby command ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ supplies a clear intended orientation, against which this branch's turning-away sense can be heard. It does not itself name a path, so the contrast is thematic rather than literal.

before: a force that turns people away,
after: a force acting against a course marked by clear proofs
reason: Moses comes with بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ immediately after this account, giving the surah a clear-evidence direction beside the earlier diversion. Proofs are not a road word themselves, so they provide a strong contextual contrast rather than a second literal path.

before: the one who diverts from a course,
after: an image aligned with the Fatiha's astray group
reason: ش ط ن B003 gives departure from an intended direction, and the Fatiha names ٱلضَّآلِّينَ, those astray, after asking for the straight path. This recited phrase activates the branch's misdirection image as a Qur'anic counterpart to فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ.

before: a force that bends or turns from direction,
after: a force heard against the straight course requested in prayer
reason: The branch includes deviation and crookedness, while ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ explicitly supplies the straight path. The contrast lets the name carry an image of turning away from the course repeatedly sought in salah.

after: a rebellious tempter who makes wrongful conduct attractive
reason: ش ط ن B004 gives the rebellious evil being, while وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ shows this agent actively beautifying the people's deeds. The following diversion from ٱلسَّبِيلِ confirms the harmful direction of that attraction, so the dictionary's rebellious quality is activated by the verse's action.

after: a being characterized by its influence on people's conduct
reason: أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ makes conduct the object of the adversary's beautification, providing a behavioral trace for the branch's evil rebel. Since the noun deeds is neutral by itself, the surrounding verb is needed to color it.

after: a faint opening toward the human kind of devil
reason: B004 explicitly allows a human rebel to be called a shaytan, and لِلنَّاسِ supplies an actual human-population word in the same surah. Those people are not called rebellious in that verse, so this only weakly activates the human extension.

after: a faint irascible coloring from the angered group
reason: The Fatiha's ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ supplies an anger image beside the branch's unruly, hostile being. The word names those subjected to anger rather than an angry devil, so the link is weak.

after: a faint contrast with the servant's obedience
reason: The Fatiha says إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ, placing exclusive service beside this branch's rebellious creature. That contrast can sharpen the rebellion image, though worship does not itself name a rebel.

after: a faint ugly-creature image set against beautification
reason: B005 gives an ugly snake or plant called shaytan, while وَزَيَّنَ says that the adversary beautified the deeds. The direct beauty-versus-ugliness contrast is striking, but the verse names no snake, plant, or grotesque head.

before: the shaytan name with an ugly-creature branch,
after: a faint unpleasantness coloring for the ugly form
reason: The word سِىٓءَ describes Lot being distressed, giving a nearby unpleasant-affect word that can brush against the branch's ugly appearance. It describes his state rather than an ugly creature, so it is a weak trigger.

after: a second hearing as the ugly snake named shaytan
reason: B005 preserves an ugly serpent called shaytan, and the Fatiha's ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ calls the proposed irritable, sullen serpent image through its anger word. The familiar adversary remains primary, while the snake image is a possible secondary hearing joined by that trigger.

before: a shaytan name with an ugly-form branch,
after: a weak contrast with creation's balanced form
reason: The bridge pairs the ugly creature branch with خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ and the dictionary's complete, balanced form sense. Creation itself is not described as deformed, so the contrast offers only a secondary image.

trigger_ar: بَيْتًا وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ
before: their dwellings remain visible evidence of ruin,
after: a second dwelling image exposes how shelter can fail
reason: The focus calls the ruined peoples' مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ evidence open to the audience. The next verse repeats the dwelling image with بَيْتًا and أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ, making the spider's fragile house a new contrast to the surviving testimony of ruined homes.
